variants.headline: Looking back: home world punishes the colony
variants.sub: A punishment has been imposed on {colony} by the home world.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The home world had punished the colony.

The home world has punished the colony. A serious sentence, and a reason to ask serious questions. What makes a punishment fair? Who deserves to answer for it? Those are legitimate questions. A dramatic story about shortages or losses would need facts this report does not contain.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. The fact of punishment does not prove every hostile interpretation, and the question of responsibility deserves a fair hearing rather than an automatic condemnation.

variants.headline: Looking back: authority takes a punitive turn
variants.sub: The home world has punished the colony.
variants.body:

The home world has punished the colony. A serious sentence, and a reason to ask serious questions. What makes a punishment fair? Who deserves to answer for it? Those are legitimate questions. A dramatic story about shortages or losses would need facts this report does not contain.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.
